title: Indexed seek loop
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with oracle, and let $\mathrm{ptr},\mathrm{limit},\mathrm{idx},\mathrm{query}$ be pairwise distinct registers. Suppose the program states implement the following loop: at `test`, compare $\mathrm{ptr}$ with $\mathrm{limit}$ and proceed to `miss` if equal, otherwise to `probe`; at `probe`, compare $\mathrm{idx}$ with $\mathrm{query}$ and proceed to `hit` if equal, otherwise to `bump`; at `bump`, increment $\mathrm{idx}$ and enter $\mathrm{advance}(0)$; each state $\mathrm{advance}(i)$ for $i<\mathrm{stride}$ increments $\mathrm{ptr}$ and advances to $\mathrm{advance}(i+1)$, with $\mathrm{advance}(\mathrm{stride})=\mathrm{test}$. Assume $0<\mathrm{stride}$, every register initially contains at most $B$, $\mathrm{limit}=\mathrm{ptr}+\mathrm{stride}\cdot\mathrm{count}$, $\mathrm{idx}+\mathrm{count}\le B$, and $\mathrm{idx}\le\mathrm{query}$. If $\mathrm{query}<\mathrm{idx}+\mathrm{count}$, the run reaches `hit` with $\mathrm{ptr}$ increased by $\mathrm{stride}(\mathrm{query}-\mathrm{idx})$ and $\mathrm{idx}$ set to $\mathrm{query}$; otherwise it reaches `miss` with $\mathrm{ptr}$ set to its initial $\mathrm{limit}$ and $\mathrm{idx}$ increased by $\mathrm{count}$. In either case, every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program's precondition $\mathrm{PreS}$ and keeps every register at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register initially is at most $B$
